I read the whole file (lines 1–206). It has no new def, structure, class or abbrev, so nothing in it can be a competing version of an existing concept. It contains only these declarations:
- Instances stating `DescendsAlong` for surjective, universally closed, universally open, universally injective, isomorphisms and open immersions.
- A lemma, `HasRingHomProperty.descendsAlong_flat`.
- An instance saying fpqc descent implies fppf descent.
- Two `(Over.pullback f).Faithful` instances.
All of these use the existing `MorphismProperty.DescendsAlong`, `Over.pullback`, `Functor.Faithful`, `Surjective ⊓ Flat ⊓ QuasiCompact` and similar notions. Because they only apply existing notions, the rubric's concept-duplication question has no suitable target. Duplicated theorems and shorter proofs are excluded by the rubric. The repeated closed/open proofs are standalone proof duplication, so I did not report them. I did not search Mathlib for duplicates of the individual theorems.
